questions.stem: A school has 600 boys and 400 girls. A stratified sample of 50 students is needed. How many girls should be in the sample?
questions.explanation: In a stratified sample, each group is represented proportionally. Girls = (400/1000) × 50 = 20. Option (a) assumes equal split. The proportion of girls in the school is 40%, so 40% of the sample should be girls.

questions.stem: Which question is most suitable for a questionnaire about exercise habits?

options.text: How often do you exercise? (a lot / sometimes / never)
Don't you think exercise is important?
How many hours per week do you spend exercising? (0-2 / 3-5 / 6-8 / 9+)

questions.explanation: Option (c) has clear, non-overlapping response categories with a measurable unit (hours per week). Option (a) uses vague terms. Option (b) is a leading question. Option (d) has no response options.

questions.stem: A factory produces 200 items per hour. A systematic sample of every 20th item is checked. How many items are sampled per hour?
questions.explanation: 200 ÷ 20 = 10 items per hour. Systematic sampling selects items at regular intervals from an ordered list. This gives a spread across the entire production run.

questions.stem: A survey response box has options: 0-10, 10-20, 20-30. What is wrong with these categories?

options.text: The categories overlap (e.g., 10 fits in two groups)

questions.explanation: A value of exactly 10 could be placed in '0-10' or '10-20'. Categories should not overlap. Better options would be: 0-9, 10-19, 20-29 or 0 < x <= 10, 10 < x <= 20, etc.

questions.stem: A company has 80 managers, 200 office staff and 120 warehouse workers. For a stratified sample of 40, how many warehouse workers should be selected?
questions.explanation: Total employees = 80 + 200 + 120 = 400. Warehouse proportion = 120/400 = 0.3. Sample from warehouse = 40 × 0.3 = 12.
